problem: End-to-end VLM navigation policies struggle with long-horizon navigation and lack dynamic reasoning, while zero-shot MLLM pipelines have weak spatial grounding and are slow. Prior dual-system methods only coarsely combine the two paradigms without strengthening spatial capability in either system.
motivation: Spatial awareness (sense of direction, passage connectivity, geometry) is abstract and easily overlooked, yet it directly affects success in long-horizon VLN-CE. The authors want a fast VLM to handle low-level actions while a slow MLLM adds global spatial reasoning, with both systems explicitly spatially enhanced.
key_idea: A fast-slow dual system in which a StreamVLN-style VLM is enhanced with implicit 3D-feature alignment (VGGT) and passage-mask tokens, and a slow GPT-4o planner picks frontier waypoints from a real-time 3D top-down map and rendered path views.
insight: Aligning intermediate-to-deep VLM layers (layer 24 best) with VGGT features gives large gains (R2R SR 61.3 to 67.3; RxR SR 58.5 to 63.9), and removing the passage-connectivity tokens (LSES) drops SR by 3.5 on R2R and 4.1 on RxR. The dual system beats either system alone (S1 62.8 / S2 59.8 SR on R2R vs 67.3), and System 2 alone is about 6x slower (294 s vs 57 s), so running S1 at 20:1 relative to S2 balances SR and time.
method: System 1 backbone: StreamVLN-style LLaVA-Video-7B (Qwen2-7B) that predicts low-level actions from RGB streams, using multi-turn dialogue, KV cache and voxel-based spatial token pruning.

Global Spatial Enhancement Strategy: at an intermediate attention layer, visual tokens go through a 2-layer MLP with BN and are aligned by cosine distance to VGGT spatial features plus positional embeddings; loss L = L_action + alpha * mean(1 - cos).

Local Spatial Enhancement Strategy (Channel Connectivity Extraction): Grounding DINO detects passages (corridors, doors), SAM segments them into binary masks (passage=1, else 0), and an MLP projects them into extra tokens matching the global visual tokens.
System 2 Mapping: builds a lightweight online 3D map with the feed-forward LingBot-Map and a 2D frontier map following VLFM.

System 2 Rendering: projects frontier points into the 3D map, plans A* paths from the agent, interpolates poses along each path, renders virtual-camera RGB views, and prunes redundant views via CLIP cosine similarity below threshold tau.

System 2 Reasoning: GPT-4o first describes location, relations and possible directions from the 3D top-down map, then compares the rendered image sequences for each frontier path with the instruction and picks the best frontier waypoint.
Fast-slow scheduler: System 1 executes many low-level actions while System 2 reasons; the agent then follows the planned waypoint, with S1:S2 frequency ratio 20:1 chosen.

setting.backbone: System 1: LLaVA-Video-7B (Qwen2-7B) fine-tuned; System 2: GPT-4o (frozen, training-free) with LingBot-Map, VGGT for supervision, Grounding DINO + SAM
setting.training_data: Oracle VLN trajectories for 1 epoch, then DAgger-collected trajectories plus VLN data and general multimodal data for another epoch; about 2000 A100 GPU hours; System 2 needs no training
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (System 2 additionally builds a 3D map online from RGB)
setting.action_space: low-level discrete: MOVE FORWARD 0.25 m, TURN LEFT/RIGHT 15°, STOP; System 2 outputs frontier waypoints

numbers.extra: DAgger + general multimodal data; S1:S2 frequency 20:1; RGB only

results: SEDualVLN reaches R2R-CE val-unseen SR 67.3 / SPL 62.5 / NE 3.75 and RxR-CE SR 63.9 / SPL 52.4 / nDTW 72.8 using only monocular RGB. This beats DualVLN (64.3 / 58.5 SR/SPL on R2R; 61.4 SR on RxR) and StreamVLN (56.9 SR).
limitations: Real-robot deployment is not shown; real-time 3D mapping is distorted in the real world, which degrades the whole system
System 2 depends on a large proprietary MLLM (GPT-4o) and is slow (about 294 s per episode alone), and training is costly (about 2000 A100 hours)
The pipeline is complex, relying on many external models (VGGT, Grounding DINO, SAM, LingBot-Map, CLIP)
